newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe starts fraud probe of war victims' fund.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe starts fraud probe of war victims' fund.

text.p: A judicial commission began a probe on Monday of allegations of massive fraud in Zimbabwe's war victims' compensation fund.
The fund was set up to assist former fighters still suffering the effects of the country's 1970s bush war which ended with independence from Britain in 1980.
But allegations of heavy fraud, including accusations that some was perpetrated by cabinet ministers, prompted President Robert Mugabe to set up the commission.

Finnie Munyira, a former secretary in the public service, labour and social welfare ministry under which the fund fell, told the 11-member commission the atmosphere for those working with the fund had been intimidating, but did not give details.

Munyira also told the hearing that Vice President Joshua Nkomo, his wife and opposition politician Edgar Tekere had benefited from a "fast track" plan under which some applicants for compensation had been given preferential treatment.
Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Florence Chitauro told the commission that weak legislation had led to looting of the multi-million dollar state fund.
Ex-combatants, intended to be the beneficiaries of the fund, say they are suffering and have demonstrated several times in the last few months.
They have marched on Mugabe's official residence and offices, held ministers hostage and even threatened lynchings.
